title: Two Laredo Men Sentenced to Federal Prison in Card-Skimming Scheme That Hit More Than 1,500 Cards
excerpt: Two Laredo men are headed to federal prison after a credit card fraud scheme that compromised more than 1,500 credit and debit card numbers — including the gove
content:
Two Laredo men are headed to federal prison after a credit card fraud scheme that compromised more than 1,500 credit and debit card numbers — including the government travel card of a U.S. Customs and Border Protection special agent.

U.S. District Judge Ivan L.R. Lemelle sentenced Liover Leon-Hernandez, 33, to 46 months in federal prison and Orlandi Castillo Leon, 35, to 37 months. Both men are Cuban nationals living in Laredo, and both are expected to face removal proceedings after completing their sentences.

Leon and Leon-Hernandez pleaded guilty — on April 8 and May 6, respectively — to possessing 15 or more counterfeit or unauthorized access devices with intent to defraud and to knowingly using other people’s identifying information without lawful authority.

How the scheme unraveled

The investigation began on March 31, 2025, after a CBP special agent reported fraudulent charges on his government travel card at a grocery store in Laredo — even though the card was still in his possession in Houston.

Surveillance footage later captured the two men using seven credit or debit accounts belonging to other people to buy gift cards and personal items. Investigators traced multiple victims’ card information to a common point of purchase and found a skimming device installed in a gas pump at a local Valero station.

On July 16, 2025, authorities executed search warrants at the men’s shared residence. During the search, Leon-Hernandez tried to swallow a thumb drive containing 1,530 stolen card numbers. Agents also recovered a magnetic stripe card reader-writer, gift cards, money orders and a counterfeit American Express card encoded with an Illinois customer’s account information.

The investigation was conducted by the FBI and the CBP Office of Professional Responsibility, with help from the Laredo Police Department and the Texas Financial Crimes Intelligence Center. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Ann Booth Zeller and Henry Thomas Sekula prosecuted the case.

What it means for Laredo

The case is a reminder that card skimming at gas pumps and stores remains active in the Laredo area — and that even a federal agent’s card was not immune. Authorities have not said whether additional suspects are being sought.

Sources: U.S. Department of Justice, via World Lawyers Forum, Nov. 19, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 20, 2026.
